AC-1 EVIDENCE — DIRECT ANTHROPIC live structured cache canary: RAN, PASSED.

Instrument: a throwaway out-of-tree script driving PydanticAIRunner.run() with
mode=structured, output_schema=completion_verdict, execution_mode=single_turn, over a
byte-identical 41,360-char system prefix (~10.7k tokens, well above the model's documented
1024-token minimum cacheable prefix). Two calls: call 1 = cache WRITE, call 2 = cache READ.
No credential was printed, logged, or persisted; only model ids and integer counts were
captured.

Model id (requested and ran): anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6
Provider provenance: provider=anthropic, tier=first_class, prompt_cache_style=anthropic,
cache_min_prefix_tokens=1024, cache settings emitted =
{anthropic_cache_instructions: true, anthropic_cache_tool_definitions: true}
Typed result: verdict=PASS (a valid completion_verdict; keys criteria/findings/summary/verdict)
Runner provenance: pydantic_ai

CALL 1 (write) — started 2026-08-20T00:10:29.995799+00:00, finished 2026-08-20T00:10:52.378397+00:00
  requests            = 1
  input_tokens        = 10759
  output_tokens       = 35
  cache_write_tokens  = 10697
  cache_read_tokens   = 0
  finish_reason       = stop
  output_retry_allowance = 2 (none consumed)

CALL 2 (read) — started 2026-08-20T00:10:52.378410+00:00, finished 2026-08-20T00:10:56.002320+00:00
  requests            = 1
  input_tokens        = 10759
  output_tokens       = 35
  cache_write_tokens  = 0
  cache_read_tokens   = 10697
  finish_reason       = stop
  output_retry_allowance = 2 (none consumed)

COMPLETE-vs-OMIT BRANCH — observed directly, not inferred. The seam-1 wire-projection
capability was instrumented so every before_model_request invocation reported its own
decision. On each of the two calls it fired exactly once with:
  messages_in = 1, messages_kept = 1, failed_output_candidates = 0, omitted = 0,
  output reserve = 16000 tokens, candidate set = ["anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6"]
=> the COMPLETE branch was taken on every request; nothing was omitted. The OMIT branch was
not exercised, because no failed intermediate output response existed to project (the first
response was well-formed both times) — which is exactly what the contract predicts for a
happy-path run, not a gap in the measurement.

AC-2 EVIDENCE — BEDROCK live structured cache canary: RAN, PASSED.

Same instrument, same byte-identical 41,360-char system prefix, same two-call write/read

CALL 2 (read) — started 2026-08-20T00:11:15.106583+00:00, finished 2026-08-20T00:11:16.925353+00:00
  requests            = 1
  input_tokens        = 10747
  output_tokens       = 34
  cache_write_tokens  = 0
  cache_read_tokens   = 10685
  finish_reason       = stop
  output_retry_allowance = 2 (none consumed)

COMPLETE-vs-OMIT BRANCH — same direct instrumentation. On each call the wire projection fired
exactly once with messages_in = 1, messages_kept = 1, failed_output_candidates = 0,
omitted = 0, reserve = 16000 tokens, candidate set = ["bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6"]
=> COMPLETE branch on every request, nothing omitted; the OMIT branch was not exercised for
the same happy-path reason as the Anthropic arm.

MEASUREMENT CAVEAT (recorded so it is not mistaken for a finding). The canary additionally
probed capabilities out-of-band by passing the model STRING "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-
sonnet-4-6", and that probe reported prompt_cache_style="none" with no cache settings. That is
an artifact of the STRING form: bedrock deliberately has no string profile resolver (resolving
one would require boto3), so a bedrock string lands on the conservative record. The runner's
own path passes the model OBJECT, which resolves the real Bedrock profile — and the live
counts prove it did: a 10,685-token cache WRITE followed by a 10,685-token cache READ cannot
occur with caching disabled. Do not read that probe line as a Bedrock caching defect.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
AC-3 CROSS-CHECK — observed accounting vs the documented contract in docs/llm-framework.md
section "The structured retry layers and their accounting (one bounded operation)", count by
count, over the four live calls above (2 Anthropic + 2 Bedrock).

1. "exactly one outer Agent.run_sync per output mode" / "exactly one on a well-formed first
   response" — MATCHES. requests = 1 on all four calls, finish_reason = stop, typed
   completion_verdict returned each time. No call recorded a second model request.

2. Output-repair allowance N = min(OUTPUT_RETRIES, max(0, structured_retry_limit)) —
   MATCHES as to the value. output_retry_allowance resolved to 2 on all four calls (the
   documented default OUTPUT_RETRIES, with structured_retry_limit unset). Zero of that
   allowance was consumed, consistent with requests = 1.

3. Transport retry "does not add a model request to the usage tally" — NOT EXERCISED. No
   HTTP-layer failure occurred, so no transport resend happened. Recorded as unexercised
   rather than claimed as confirmed.

4. native->prompted downgrade is "the only sanctioned second outer run_sync" — NOT TRIGGERED,
   and consistently so: native structured output is supported on both models, no grammar
   rejection occurred, and requests = 1 rules out a second outer run.

5. "Complete-or-omit history ... an over-budget failed response is omitted whole, never
   truncated" — the COMPLETE branch MATCHES and is directly observed (see the two evidence
   comments: 1 message in, 1 kept, 0 omitted, on every request). The OMIT branch is
   structurally unreachable on a well-formed first response, because it only applies to a
   failed intermediate output response, of which there were none. Unexercised, not divergent.

6. "Trace, not usage, for candidates" — NOT EXERCISED. Each canary arm ran a single-candidate
   model, so no fallback candidate was attempted and discarded; there was nothing for the
   trace to hold apart from usage.

7. CACHE READ / WRITE / INPUT relationship — MATCHES, identically on both providers, and
   confirms the inclusive-input convention rebar documents (docs/ci-provider-matrix.md
   footnote 1: input_tokens as logged is inclusive of cache read and cache write, so billable
   uncached input is input - cache_read - cache_write):
     Anthropic call 1: 10759 - 0     - 10697 = 62 uncached
     Anthropic call 2: 10759 - 10697 - 0     = 62 uncached
     Bedrock   call 1: 10747 - 0     - 10685 = 62 uncached
     Bedrock   call 2: 10747 - 10685 - 0     = 62 uncached
   All four resolve to the same 62 uncached input tokens — the non-cached user turn — with the
   byte-identical prefix moving cleanly from the write column to the read column between call
   1 and call 2. The two providers differ by 12 tokens on the same prefix (10759 vs 10747),
   i.e. tokenizer/serialization overhead, not an accounting discrepancy.

VERDICT: on every count the happy path can exercise, the observed accounting matches the
documented contract. No divergence was found in the canary runs themselves.

ONE DIVERGENCE FOUND ELSEWHERE, filed rather than reconciled: this session's own plan-review
gate run on this ticket recorded 32 LLM calls, 785,178 input tokens, cache_read_tokens = 0 and
cache_write_tokens = 0, with provider provenance prompt_cache_style = "none" over the candidate
chain ["bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6", "anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6"]. That zeroing
is deliberate and already explained in rebar.toml and in runner_support._intersect_capabilities
(a mixed-provider chain collapses to "none" because the two providers' cache keys are not
interchangeable) — it is NOT a bug and NOT a contradiction of the canary results. But the
accounting section of docs/llm-framework.md, which is the section this criterion cross-checks
against, does not mention it, so an operator reconciling a real 0/0 gate run against that
section has no explanation there. Filed as a documentation follow-up, linked discovered_from
this ticket.

## Context / Problem
RP-01 S5 (`ripening-liberal-tuatara`, `10a3-7dd0-1b3d-47cc`) made the one-operation Pydantic
structured-output path authoritative. Its AC-6 is `[operator-attested]`: direct-Anthropic and
Bedrock same-run retry/cache canaries. That AC could NOT be executed in the autonomous
implementation session because live provider credentials were absent, so S5 closed with an
honest `--force` override and the contract stayed pinned only by the offline AC-1/3/4 oracle.
The credentials are now present in this environment (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` for the direct arm;
ambient AWS credentials for Bedrock), so the deferred live evidence can finally be produced.

## Approach
Drive the authoritative one-operation structured path twice per provider over a byte-identical,
cache-eligible system prefix, and record the usage the runner itself reports. Two calls, not
one: the first is the cache WRITE, the second the READ — the only shape in which a cache hit is
observable at all (the same two-call shape the existing live Bedrock canary uses,
`tests/external/test_bedrock_cache_live.py::test_bedrock_repeated_prefix_hits_cache`).

Concretely, per provider:
1. Build `LLMConfig(model=<provider model>, repo_path=<temp dir>, runner="pydantic_ai")`
   (`src/rebar/llm/config.py`). Anthropic arm: the resolved `standard` model class via
   `rebar.llm.model_classes.resolve_model_string("standard")`. Bedrock arm:
   `"bedrock:" + rebar.llm.bedrock_model.DEFAULT_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID`.
2. Submit `RunRequest(mode="structured", output_schema="completion_verdict",
   execution_mode="single_turn", reviewers=[], system_prompt=<identical padding>, …)` through
   `PydanticAIRunner(cfg).run(req)` — the single `get_runner(...).run(...)` facade
   (`src/rebar/llm/runner.py:80` for the request fields; `completion_verdict` is a registered
   contract, `src/rebar/llm/contracts.py:289`).
3. Read the observed counts off `result["_usage"]`, which `runner.py:672` sets from
   `structured_run._extract_usage` (`src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:479`) — the dict carries
   exactly `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`, and
   `requests`, i.e. every count this ticket must record, with no new instrumentation.
4. Observe the complete-vs-omit branch directly rather than inferring it: wrap the projection
   callable built by `rebar.llm.pai_retry._make_wire_projection` (attached as the seam-1
   `ProcessHistory` capability by `structured_run.apply_structured_seams`,
   `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:181`) so each `before_model_request` invocation records how
   many messages entered, how many were kept, and whether any failed-output `ModelResponse` was
   omitted by `_wire_keeps_response` (`src/rebar/llm/pai_retry.py:177`).

The system prefix is sized well above the model's documented minimum cacheable prefix
(`capabilities.CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS` / `_cache_min_prefix_tokens`,
`src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py:87`), because below that floor a zero/zero cache reading is the
EXPECTED result and would prove nothing either way.

Why this approach fits: the counts to be attested are already computed and surfaced by
production code on the very path under test, so the canary observes the real seam instead of
re-deriving it; and running it as a throwaway out-of-tree script rather than a new committed
test keeps a billable, credential-dependent probe out of CI, where `tests/external/` is already
the sanctioned home for anything live and no new permanent live test is being asked for here.

## Scope
No repository files change. This is an evidence-production task: the canary is a throwaway
script created under a temporary directory OUTSIDE the checkout and deleted after the run, and
all output lands on this ticket. File impact is declared `none` with that reason.

## Testing
- Direct-Anthropic arm: two identical-prefix structured calls; record both runs' full usage
  dicts, the resolved model id, and the projection decisions.
- Bedrock arm: the same two-call sequence against `bedrock:<DEFAULT_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID>`.
- Failure path is a first-class outcome, not an abort: if either arm raises (missing/invalid
  credential, region error, model-access denial, provider error), the exact error class and
  message are recorded on the ticket as the observed result for that arm and that arm's
  criterion is left UNCHECKED — a blocked provider is never inferred from the other's success.
- Cross-check: compare each arm's observed `requests`, `cache_read_tokens`,
  `cache_write_tokens`, and `input_tokens` against `docs/llm-framework.md` §"The structured
  retry layers and their accounting (one bounded operation)" — exactly one outer run on a
  well-formed first response, transport retry adding no model request, candidates traced but
  not folded into usage — and against `rebar.llm.cache_diagnostics.warn_if_cache_ineffective`'s
  stated expectation (`src/rebar/llm/cache_diagnostics.py:88`).
- Secret hygiene: nothing in the canary prints, logs, or persists a credential; only model ids
  and integer counts are recorded.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] [operator-attested] Direct Anthropic canary: a live structured run over the authoritative one-operation path succeeds with a typed result; the ticket records timestamp, model id, request count, cache read/write/input counts, and the complete-vs-omit branch; no secret appears in output or artifacts. Checked by reading the recorded evidence comment on this ticket: it names the model id and carries integer counts for `requests`, `cache_read_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`, and `input_tokens` for both calls.
  provenance: environment=local macOS developer workstation (Darwin 25.5.0), rebar worktree venv; principal=the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY-authenticated Anthropic account configured in this shell, unnamed and never read or emitted by the canary; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — two real billable calls were made to anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6 through the same runner facade and the same credential environment variable rebar's own gates use, and the recorded counts are the runner's own reported usage, not a simulation or a re-derivation.
- [x] [operator-attested] Direct Bedrock canary: the same live two-call sequence over Bedrock, recorded the same way and checked the same way.
  provenance: environment=local macOS developer workstation (Darwin 25.5.0), AWS region us-west-2; principal=AWS account 896586841071 assumed via the ambient AWS credential chain (profile `frontier`); privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — two real billable calls were made to bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 on the same account, region, and ambient-credential path this project's LLM gates run on, and the recorded counts are the runner's own reported usage.
- [x] The observed cache read/write/input accounting is compared, count by count, against `docs/llm-framework.md` §"The structured retry layers and their accounting (one bounded operation)", and the ticket records either an explicit "matches" statement per count or a follow-up ticket linked `discovered_from` this one for each divergence. Checked by reading that comparison comment on this ticket and, where a divergence exists, resolving the linked follow-up ticket id. Result: the seven-point comparison is recorded as a comment; every count the happy path exercises matches, the unexercised branches are named as unexercised rather than claimed, and the one divergence found (the accounting section not mentioning that a mixed-provider fallback chain resolves to no prompt caching) is filed as `imperious-latticed-xenopus` (d763-944e-c66d-4ac2), linked `discovered_from` this ticket.

Where output or evidence lives: the observed timestamps, model ids, request counts, cache read/write/input counts, complete-vs-omit projection decisions, and the docs/llm-framework.md cross-check are recorded as comments on ticket f91e-57a2-f790-4ebd, with any divergence filed as a follow-up ticket linked discovered_from it.
